blocks.text: The video separates two jobs that are often confused: reading a physical PlayStation 2 disc into an ISO and compressing that image into CHD for emulation. It describes routes for Windows, macOS and Linux and names the tools used. A clean source dump matters more than the compression ratio, since a converter cannot repair unreadable sectors or a truncated image. The guide is relevant to maintaining a lawful personal backup workflow.

Only dump discs you own and check the law that applies to you. Keep the original image until the compressed result passes verification and boots in the intended emulator. Record disc title, region and revision so a later filename change does not erase identity; compare file size and checksums before deleting a working copy. The video demonstrates a practical sequence, but drive quality and disc damage can change results, and a successful first menu does not prove every part of an image is intact.
